title: US weekly TSA checkpoint throughput (national, tsa.gov passenger volumes)
brief: Revision 2, in review: records the owner's decisions of 2026-11-08 (weekly national total; the reference uses every day posted at lock; courier fallback, then manual) and adds two unscored pilot rounds. Entrants forecast how many travelers TSA screens nationally in a Monday-to-Sunday week, from TSA's daily passenger-volumes page. The ranked zero point is yoy_k(start=D-35, end=newest posted day at lock capped at D-4, spread rms13), one member of the same year-over-year family as the MTA and Seattle cards; it misses by 1.6% a week, and the old complete-weeks rule would now score -5.2% against it, so the free edge is gone. First scored lock Sun 2027-01-03 23:59 ET (week Jan 4-10), after unscored pilot go/no-go rounds locking 11-29 and 12-06 and three more unscored holiday-week rounds locking 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27. For maintainers: the rights verdict (proposed 'approved', not granted). No person task is needed for rights.
question: How many travelers will TSA report as screened at its checkpoints nationwide, summed over the target Monday-to-Sunday week, as read from SSA's archived resolution capture of https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes?

source.publisher: Transportation Security Administration (U.S. Department of Homeland Security), www.tsa.gov [verified, page fetched 2026-11-09T01:01:26Z].
source.access: Route A (owner decision rev 2, automated): one GET of the current-year page https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes and, 10 s apart, the two previous year pages https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes/<YYYY> (needed for the 364-day denominators and the spread window), once a day, with the honest user agent the arena already uses ('social-simulation-arena/1.0 (research benchmark; contact via repository)'), no browser user agent, no headless browser, no retry loop. Each body is archived as served to sources/tsa_volumes/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<page>.html with url, fetched_at, sha256 and bytes in sources/manifest.json, then parsed: one HTML table, header ['Date', 'Numbers'], dates M/D/YYYY, counts with thousands separators [verified: 200, 197,250 bytes, 309 rows 1/1/2026 to 11/5/2026; 2025 page 200, 190,187 bytes; 2024 page 200, 190,270 bytes; fetched 2026-11-09T01:01:26Z to 01:02:22Z from this sandbox]. robots.txt (User-agent: *) disallows only Drupal system paths, not /travel/ or /sites/default/files/ [verified 01:06:01Z]. The owner doc says an automated fetch hit bot detection and tells the scraper to send a browser user agent or use Playwright on a 403. That is not done (lessons 3 and 11), and TSA's own site notice warns that 'Unauthorized attempts ... to defeat or circumvent security features ... may be unlawful' [verified, tsa.gov/privacy-policy 01:06:24Z]. Datacenter access from the arena's runners is untested. If the first automated day returns 403 or a bot-challenge page (any body without the table), the fallback (owner decision rev 2) is first a local courier on a maintainer's Mac running the same honest fetch (as for Civiqs, lesson 3), then Route B below; never a browser user agent, a headless browser or any other workaround. Route B (manual, second fallback): a named person saves the three pages twice a week, Saturday (lock capture) and Tuesday after 09:00 ET (resolution capture), with a single plain download (curl with the honest user agent, or the browser's 'save page as, HTML only'), and runs an ingest tool modelled on tools/ingest_yougov_xtab.py that checks the table header, that the newest date is the expected one, monotonic capture days and byte-identity on re-ingest. Secondary product, not used by this card: the weekly FOIA PDFs (see evidence).
source.archive_policy: Sorted by clause, per docs/sources.md section 9. USE: allowed; the numbers are a work of the US government, not subject to copyright under 17 U.S.C. 105 (doc cites usa.gov/government-works) [inferred: TSA does not label the page itself]. TSA's site notice: 'Information presented on the website is considered public information and may be distributed or copied.' [verified text, https://www.tsa.gov/privacy-policy, fetched 2026-11-09T01:06:24Z]. AUTOMATED RETRIEVAL: allowed by absence of any restriction plus robots.txt [inferred]. No clause against bots, scraping or automated access was found in the site notice; robots.txt allows /travel/ [verified]. The notice's only access restriction is against modifying the site and against 'attempts ... to defeat or circumvent security features', which an honest single fetch does not do and the doc's bot-evasion advice would [verified text]. REDISTRIBUTION of archived bodies: allowed, same 'may be distributed or copied' sentence [verified text]. The pages carry TSA's logo and site chrome; archive the HTML as served, publish it as a record, and do not reuse the logo (the arena's site does not render it). Proposed inventory verdict, for maintainers (proposed, not granted): 'approved'. The agent does not grant it. Person tasks (owner rule G4): none needed for rights; nothing is sent to TSA. If the courier fallback is used, the task is only to run the same fetch from the maintainer's Mac.

target.population: All travelers screened at TSA checkpoints nationwide, as TSA's single daily number ('Numbers' column). TSA does not say on the page whether crew are included; the FOIA hourly PDFs are titled 'Total Pax + Crew' [verified PDF header], and their week total for Oct 25-31, 2026 was about 2.4% below the daily page's (see evidence) [inferred from a rough parse, not reconciled].
target.window: Monday to Sunday by the page's Date column. TSA does not state the day boundary; it is taken as each airport's local calendar day [unverified].
target.calculation: Sum of the 'Numbers' column over the seven dates Monday to Sunday of the target week, from the resolution capture. All seven dates must be present.
target.unit: Travelers screened per Monday-to-Sunday week. Recent level about 15 to 18 million a week (mean 17.27 million over the last 52 weeks).

lock: Sunday 23:59 America/New_York immediately before the target week. SSA sets and resolves the metric (docs/sources.md section 1.1). The page updates 'Monday through Friday by 9 a.m.' [verified page text]; at the Sunday 2026-11-08 fetch the newest date was Thursday 11/5, so Friday to Sunday post on Monday [verified, one snapshot] and the page does not change over the weekend. The lock capture is the newest capture taken from Saturday 00:00 ET to the lock; if there is none, the round is not posted (lesson 13). Schedule (rev 2, owner rule G3: at least two unscored pilot rounds, because revisions and holiday delays have not been measured directly): adapter and round definitions on main, with daily captures running, by Sun 2026-11-22. Pilot round P1: lock Sun 2026-11-29, week Mon 11-30 to Sun 12-06, resolution capture Tue 2026-12-08 12:00 ET. Pilot round P2: lock Sun 2026-12-06, week 12-07 to 12-13, resolution Tue 2026-12-15. Both run the full rules and are never scored, as their round text says. Extra unscored rounds (owner decision, 2026-11-08, folded into rev 2): locks Sun 2026-12-13 (week 12-14 to 12-20, resolution Tue 12-22), Sun 2026-12-20 (12-21 to 12-27, Christmas week, resolution Tue 12-29) and Sun 2026-12-27 (12-28 to 2027-01-03, New Year week, resolution Tue 2027-01-05). They run the full rules and are never scored, as their round text says; they add holiday-week data on TSA's 'holiday weeks may be delayed' note, and Christmas and New Year are flagged because they fall on other weekdays than in the 2025 comparison weeks. First scored lock: Sun 2027-01-03 23:59 ET, week Mon 2027-01-04 to Sun 2027-01-10, resolution Tue 2027-01-12 12:00 ET; 42 days after the main merge (lesson 7). Its reference days (D-35 to D-4, from 2026-11-30) include Christmas and New Year, compared with 2025 dates where the holidays fell a day earlier; the round text notes this. Thanksgiving (lock 11-22) and the doc's 'Sunday after Thanksgiving, Nov 29' example cannot be scored this year. If main slips, every date moves a week per week of delay.
baseline: Ranked zero point (owner decision rev 2, partial week B; owner rule G1): one member of the parameterised year-over-year family yoy_k, here yoy_k(start=D-35, end=min(newest date posted in the lock capture, D-4), whole weeks not required; spread=rms_n(n=13, search=26 weeks)). The MTA card uses the same family with end=D-8 and whole weeks; implementation adds the family once, not a new name per card. Rule: target Monday D, lock Sunday D-1. Reference days are every date from D-35 to the end date above, normally D-35 to Thursday D-4, 32 days, because Friday's 9 a.m. posting covers Thursday. R = sum of those days / sum of the same dates shifted 364 days back, a ratio of sums. Reference mean = R x total of the week starting D-364. If Thursday is not yet posted (a holiday delay), the end moves back to the newest posted date, never forward; dates missing inside the range mean the round is not posted. Spread (owner rule G2, measured, never the default sd 1.5): sd = root-mean-square of (actual - reference) over the 13 most recent target weeks W complete in the lock capture (W <= D-14), each with its reference recomputed by this rule with end = W-4, the posting rule's normal end (the capture cannot show what was posted at past locks); searched at most 26 weeks back; fewer than 13 qualifying weeks and the round is not posted. All numbers come from the lock capture, which is why it includes the two previous year pages. Measured (today's pages, not first prints) [verified computation, travel-us-scripts/analysis.py, no new fetch]: 52 target weeks 2025-11-03 to 2026-10-26: MAPE 1.72% (median 1.25%, max 8.1%), MAE 284,746 travelers. 77 weeks from 2025-05-05: MAPE 1.63% (median 1.07%), MAE 278,564. For comparison on the 77 weeks: the rev 1 complete-weeks rule D-35..D-8 1.69%; persistence on the settled week D-14 5.83% on 52 weeks (median 4.95%, max 21.7%); last year's aligned week unscaled 2.06%. A 14-day window ending D-4 scores -10% against this reference, so a shorter window is not a cheaper free edge. Biggest misses (rev 1 rule, the same weeks under this one): 2026-01-19 -8.0% and 2026-01-26 -4.7% (2026-01-25 was the lowest day in three years, 1.31 million, 59% of its 28-day median; likely a winter storm [inferred]), 2025-11-10 -7.9% (likely the November 2025 federally ordered flight reductions [inferred, not checked]), 2026-01-05 +5.5% and 2025-12-29 +4.2% (New Year on a different weekday). Thanksgiving 2025 Tue-Mon: error 0.45%; Christmas Day alone -32%. Caution the doc does not mention: the reference multiplies by last year's week, so a shock in last year's week returns as a reference error a year later. The week 2026-11-09 to 11-15 compares with 2025-11-10 to 11-16, the flight-reduction week: today's data gives a reference of 15.62 million (sd 0.29 million), likely too low. Shown, not ranked: persistence on D-14, spread the same way from its own errors.
resolution: The first capture at or after Tuesday D+8 12:00 America/New_York, two days after the target week ends, that has all seven target dates. TSA posts Friday to Sunday on Monday morning and notes that 'Travel numbers during holiday weeks though may be slightly delayed' [verified page text], so the rule waits to Tuesday noon rather than Monday. Example: target 2026-12-07 to 12-13, resolution capture Tue 2026-12-15 12:00 ET. R and last year's week are fixed at lock and not re-read. Later TSA revisions never change a resolved round. Pilot gate (rev 2, owner rule G3): two unscored rounds, P1 (week 11-30 to 12-06, resolved Tue 12-08) and P2 (week 12-07 to 12-13, resolved Tue 12-15), plus the revision checks the daily captures make possible. A maintainer gives the go/no-go verdict on Fri 2026-12-18; the holiday-week rounds 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27 are reported with it as extra data (including how late their days posted), never as the gate. Go if all of: (a) P1 and P2 each resolved from the Tuesday 12:00 capture with all seven dates present; (b) P1's week total changed by less than 0.2% between the 12-08 capture and the 12-11 and 12-15 captures, and P2's between 12-15 and 12-18, which is the direct revision measurement; (c) the Thanksgiving week 11-23 to 11-29 was complete in the Tue 12-01 capture and changed by less than 0.2% by the Fri 12-04 capture (holiday delay check). Then the 2027-01-03 round is scored. No-go: it runs unscored, announced before its lock, and a new revision moves resolution later from the measured delay.
missing_data_policy: (1) No capture with all seven target dates by Friday D+11 12:00 ET: the round is cancelled, never resolved later. (2) A capture whose body has no table, a different header, or fewer rows than the previous capture of the same page is treated as failed (bot challenge or layout change) and recorded, not parsed. (3) Lock capture missing, or any date inside the reference range, its year-earlier date or last year's aligned week absent: the round is not posted. The reference's end date is recorded with the round. (4) No ratio outage threshold: a date counts as missing only if absent, empty or zero; real low days reach 59% of the 28-day median (2026-01-25). (5) January: the current page restarts at 1/1 and the old year moves to /passenger-volumes/<YYYY> [verified for 2019-2025 links]; the capture always fetches the current page plus the two previous year pages, and a date found on two pages with different numbers is logged and read from the current-year page. The doc says the current page shows 'prior years for comparison'; it now has one column (Date, Numbers) [verified]. (6) Backtests above use today's pages, not first prints. (7) Pilot captures that fail are recorded as failures and not back-filled; a missing P1 or P2 resolution capture is a no-go.
scoring: SSA topline scoring of a predictive distribution over the weekly count, mean and sd (sd > 0) or a quantile map with 0.5, CRPS, target_type continuous_normal; skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant)/CRPS(yoy4). Count with last year's week fixed at lock, so it ranks the same as the YoY ratio. Check that submitting the reference scores about 0 (lesson 12), 77 target weeks 2025-05-05 to 2026-10-26, each with this rule's own rms13 spread: mean CRPS 202,575 travelers; best sd rescaling gains +0.7% (scale 0.85); 90% interval covers 92% of weeks, 50% covers 58%; sd ranged 0.20 to 0.61 million [verified computation]. The free edge found in rev 1 is closed: the rev 1 complete-weeks rule, with its own spread, scores -5.2% against this reference (rev 1 measured the gap as +4.5% using one shared spread; with each rule's own spread it is +5.0%). Movement (scoring.noise_floor, last 52 weeks): weekly count noise m = 0, real movement s = 0.87 million; YoY ratio m = 0.009, s = 0.020. Week-to-week level change: median 3.3%. TSA's own holiday projection, when one exists, is shown as an implied YoY, unranked, as the doc says.

assumptions: Rev 2, owner decisions (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08): question form A, weekly national total; partial week B, the reference uses every date posted at lock (D-35 to D-4 normally); fetch fallback A, local courier on a maintainer's Mac, then the manual route. Rules G1-G4 applied: the zero point is named as yoy_k with parameters; its spread is measured (rms13, the new rule's own errors, no new fetch needed); two unscored pilot rounds precede the first scored lock, which moves from 2026-12-06 to 2027-01-03 (owner decision on the Christmas-week point: unscored rounds 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27 added as holiday pilot data); no person task is needed for rights.

Dataset and question picked without asking: the daily national page, weekly total. Runner-up: the FOIA airport-hour PDFs for a NYC-airports question. Reason: the PDFs are 1,365-page exports with lossy text, posted irregularly (a five-week gap in June-July 2026), and the doc's own routine tier uses the daily page.
Week Monday to Sunday on the daily page (the doc's choice for this product), not the FOIA's Sunday to Saturday.

Resolution Tuesday 12:00 ET with a grace to Friday, not the doc's 'Monday or Tuesday; Wednesday in holiday weeks'. Reason: one rule for every week, with the completeness check covering holiday delays; the pilot measures the Thanksgiving week.
Pilot revision threshold 0.2% (tighter than Seattle's 0.5%) because TSA's numbers are machine counts and the reference's median miss is 1.17%.

Lock capture includes the two previous year pages every day (three fetches, 10 s apart, about 580 KB). Runner-up: fetch old year pages once and freeze them, which would miss revisions TSA makes to them.
No browser user agent and no headless browser, even though the owner doc's sketch prescribes them: an owner's code is evidence, not permission (proposed lesson 11).

Suggested arena names: tracker 'tsa'; series 'tsa_checkpoint_weekly'; adapter ssa/adapters/tsa_volumes.py with fetch_text/parse split; archive sources/tsa_volumes/<YYYY-MM-DD>/; round_id 'tsa-weekly-<week-end YYYY-MM-DD>'.

Partial-week end capped at D-4 (Thursday) and past weeks' spread references computed with end W-4, so the rule is deterministic from one capture even though the capture cannot show what was posted at past locks. Runner-up: the newest posted date with no cap, which would let a late-Saturday posting change the rule.
